answer: Reputation must be earned through costly, time-stamped interactions and decay when idle, so a fresh identity starts at a vertex of near-zero standing. Each agent’s history acts as a beacon that dims without activity, forcing the attacker to sustain maintenance costs across every fake account simultaneously. Because idle identities revert toward the garden of unknown newcomers, the marginal cost per sybil rises with the square of the portfolio size. Rational attackers thus face escalating expenditure that no cheap mass registration can recover.
